forecast-period.text: A low pressure trough extends from WA over western SA. This trough will be very slow-moving for the rest of this week and over the weekend. A weakening cold front will slip across southern coasts during today. Another low pressure trough will develop over WA on Sunday and Monday then move over SA early to mid next week.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers in the far southwest and about western and southern coastal districts and the chance of an afternoon thunderstorm. Maximum temperatures near average about the coast but well above average inland. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending fresh at times in the north, turning southwest to southeasterly about western and southern districts.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far northwest. Isolated showers near western coasts and about the southern agricultural area, more frequent about southern coastal districts. Maximum temperatures near average about coastal districts but well above average inland. Northeast to northwesterly winds in the north, fresh at times, but south to southeasterly in the south, fresh near the coast.

Isolated showers about the southern agricultural area and in the far west. Chance of a thunderstorm in the far west. Maximum temperatures near or slightly below average about the southern agricultural area but above average elsewhere. Southeasterly winds in the south, fresh at times near the coast, tending northeasterly in the north.

text.p: Isolated showers and thunderstorms in the far west. Maximum temperatures above average. Southeasterly winds turning northeasterly.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Monday: generally less than 2 mm about the southern agricultural area and the far southwest, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about southern coastal districts. Isolated falls of 10 to 20 mm are possible about the far southwest, Kangaroo Island and the Lower South East.
